title: OpenAI to Cut Off AI Models for SpaceX-Owned Cursor
summary: OpenAI announced it will stop providing AI models to Cursor after SpaceX acquired the coding tool, escalating its feud with Elon Musk.
content: OpenAI said on August 28, 2026 that it plans to stop providing AI models to Cursor, the coding-tool company now owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX, marking a further escalation in the bitter rivalry between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Musk. OpenAI cited concerns that it 'cannot be confident that SpaceX will use our technology within our terms of service, based on our experience with Elon Musk's companies violating contracts.' The announcement drew a swift, dismissive response from Musk, who posted on X: 'I couldn't care less.' Hours later, Anthropic — which has an ongoing partnership with SpaceX — said it planned to increase compute support for its Claude models within Cursor, positioning itself to fill the gap left by OpenAI's departure. The move underscores how the intensifying personal rivalry between Altman and Musk is now reshaping the competitive landscape of AI developer tooling.

title: Tencent Open-Sources Hy4 Preview: 770B-Parameter Frontier Model
summary: Tencent released and open-sourced Hy4 Preview, a 770-billion-parameter model with a 1M+ token context window that ranks among the top open-source models globally.
content: Tencent's Hunyuan team released and open-sourced Hy4 Preview on August 28, 2026, a next-generation large language model with 770 billion total parameters, 49 billion active parameters per token, and a context window exceeding 1 million tokens. In a blind evaluation by 163 Tencent experts across 203 engineering tasks, Hy4 Preview scored 2.99 out of 4.00, edging out competitors including GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3. Notably, the model participated in its own development — for the first time in the Hunyuan series, Hy4 Preview helped automate the optimization of training methods, data strategies, and evaluation frameworks, establishing an early-stage recursive self-improvement loop. On public benchmarks, the model scored 85.4 on Terminal Bench 2.1, tying Claude Opus 5 and surpassing DeepSeek V4 Pro, and jumped from 28.0 to 64.3 on the DeepSWE real-world software engineering benchmark. The model is freely available on WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy for two weeks post-launch, and accessible via API through Tencent Cloud and OpenRouter.

title: Google Introduces Gemini 3.5 Transcribe for Intelligent Speech Recognition
summary: Google launched Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, its most accurate speech-to-text model yet, offering sub-second latency, 85-language support, and a 70% improvement in transcription speed over its predecessor.
content: Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Transcribe on August 26, 2026, its most precise speech-to-text model to date, designed to convert raw audio into polished, formatted text while handling background noise, complex jargon, and disfluency cleanup. The model achieves an average Word Error Rate of 4.0% for streaming and 2.6% for non-streaming use cases as measured by Artificial Analysis, and improves time to final transcription by 70% over the previous Chirp 3 model. It supports over 85 languages with automatic detection, multi-speaker attribution with timestamps for up to three speakers, and custom vocabulary recognition for specialized terminology. Developers can access it through two APIs: a real-time streaming API with sub-second latency for voice apps, and a pre-recorded audio processing API for meetings and call logs. The model is already powering features across Google products including Rambler on Android, the Gemini app on macOS, and Google Antigravity, with Chrome integration coming soon.

title: Salesforce and Anthropic Announce Claudeforce Enterprise Partnership
summary: Salesforce and Anthropic launched Claudeforce, a deep integration bringing Claude's reasoning directly into Salesforce CRM, Slack, and enterprise workflows.
content: Salesforce and Anthropic announced Claudeforce on August 27, 2026, an expanded strategic partnership that brings Claude's intelligence directly into Salesforce's CRM platform, Slack, and enterprise data infrastructure. The partnership launches with 'Salesforce in Claude,' a plugin featuring 37 prebuilt sales skills — including meeting prep, deal health review, and pipeline management — that let sellers take governed actions in Salesforce directly from within Claude. Powered by Salesforce's new AIforce harness, the integration connects Claude to live business data, workflows, business logic, and governance controls through MCP servers and APIs without requiring complex integrations. Claude is also now the default AI model for Slackbot across Salesforce's organization, which internally has driven 8.1 million hours of annualized productivity gains — more than doubling quarter-over-quarter. The Salesforce in Claude plugin is available to select pilot customers now, with open beta expected in September 2026.

title: Anthropic Opens Claude to 10,000 Scientists With Free Access
summary: Anthropic launched a free Claude Team plan for verified researchers and expanded its AI for Science program to all scientific fields, marking a push to make Claude foundational infrastructure for research.
content: Anthropic announced on August 27, 2026 that it is opening 10,000 free and discounted Claude Team subscription seats to scientists worldwide, with standard seats free and premium seats with five times the usage limits priced at $15 per month for verified researchers at academic or nonprofit institutions. Alongside the subscriptions, the company expanded its AI for Science credit program — previously focused on biology — to cover all scientific disciplines, including ambitious compute-heavy research projects. The announcement also confirmed that a government-linked access program for Anthropic's most restricted model tier, Mythos, has enrolled its first participants from life sciences research, with the company 'working in partnership with the US government' to provide access for biology and chemistry work with cybersecurity safeguards still in place. The moves build on Claude Science, Anthropic's AI research workbench released in beta on June 30, 2026, which integrates over 60 curated skills for fields including genomics, proteomics, and structural biology. Anthropic stated its intention to expand well beyond the initial 10,000 seats in the coming months.

title: DeepMind Completes World's First Double-Blind AI Safety Evaluation
summary: Google DeepMind conducted the first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary frontier AI model, using confidential computing to let external evaluators test Gemini without accessing its model weights.
content: Google DeepMind announced on August 29, 2026 the completion of what it describes as the world's first double-blind evaluation of a proprietary frontier AI model, testing Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite while preventing both the developer and external evaluators from accessing each other's confidential material. The experiment used Google Cloud's Confidential Space technology to place model weights and evaluation prompts inside a secure GPU enclave, allowing the model to process questions without exposing them to Google and without revealing model weights to evaluators. Partners included the Singapore AI Safety Institute, independent evaluation organization AVERI, privacy technology group OpenMined, and benchmarking consortium MLCommons, which reserved previously unreleased safety benchmark prompts specifically for this test. Remote attestation cryptographically verified that the enclave was running the agreed software configuration before any sensitive information was loaded, addressing the persistent problem of benchmark contamination where training data may include evaluation questions. The approach could become a new standard for cybersecurity, biological-risk, and government AI evaluations where data is too sensitive to share through conventional testing.
